A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hogwild! Inference research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and newly added material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original QwQ-32B experiments on grouped GSM8k questions and LIMO. Appendix A includes an original generated reasoning trace.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original mathematics and coding evaluations, component ablations, collaboration scores, and hardware runtime measurements.

M1.justification: v1 rotates cached blocks and materializes worker-specific caches layer by layer. v3 Section 3.4 introduces an optimized inference procedure that rotates current queries relative to fixed cache blocks, using one copy of each block. Section 3.3 also replaces partial in-context examples with zero-shot prompting and changes redundancy interventions from step-based to token-based scheduling. The three original cache layouts remain in Appendix A.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates grouped GSM8k and LIMO mathematics problems. v3 retains these and adds LiveCodeBench code generation, OlympiadBench text-only English mathematics and physics, and both AIME 2025 subsets. This substantially extends the evaluated domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates Skeleton-of-Thought on grouped GSM8k and LIMO, including unlimited-thread and two-thread variants in the synthetic comparison. It also adds self-consistency to the synthetic comparison and FlashAttention v2 to runtime comparisons. v1's LIMO 'Independent workers' comparator is retained under the adapted Self-Consistency name.

E3.justification: The reported LIMO evaluation changes from 512 problems, with the remainder used for development, to 817 problems; its answer-extraction limit changes from 8 to 16 tokens. The reported synthetic sample count changes from 100 to 128. v3 also introduces additional model and worker configurations, task-specific grading and answer budgets, GPT-4o collaboration scoring, and quantized-model runtime protocols.

E4.justification: v3 retains the original cache-layout ablation questions and adds removal of collaboration prompts, token re-encoding versus cache rotation, a single-worker control, scaling through six workers, and model-size sensitivity analyses in Appendix E. Section 4.3 and Appendices G–H add structured collaboration analysis and examples of interventions that help, are unnecessary, or are ignored.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates for its experiments. v3 reports averaging over eight random seeds for LiveCodeBench, ten for AIME, and three independent judge assessments per sample. Appendix F adds mean runtime and 10th/90th-percentile curves across GPUs and repetitions. These additions do not establish increased run counts for the retained v1 experiments.

E6.justification: v3 reports revised GSM8k and LIMO results under changed settings, plus extensive new benchmark, model, ablation, and collaboration results. It also adds measured runtime outcomes: Table 1 reports 19.3, 36.1, and 66.3 tokens per second for one, two, and four workers in the 8192-token column. v1 has no equivalent timing measurements; changed accuracy results should not be treated as same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: v1 states RoPE shift invariance and the cubic cost of naive re-encoding. v3 adds the blockwise attention derivation that transfers rotations from keys to queries in Section 3.4, plus query-rotation counts and complexity reasoning in Appendix B. This is a limited mathematical extension supporting the optimized computation; the underlying RoPE assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim of training-free collaboration through concurrently shared KV memory remains. v3 refines v1's few-shot feasibility claim to explicit zero-shot collaboration and gives the efficient inference implementation greater prominence. The central research contribution is retained rather than replaced.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of small-model failures, long-context and six-worker saturation, and Qwen3-14B overthinking on OlympiadBench Physics. It also explains unequal extra-token allowances in coding comparisons and limitations of proprietary, subjective collaboration judging. These substantially extend v1's largely prospective limitations discussion, although v1's specific timing-nondeterminism caveat is not retained.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's brief implementation description and selected prompt excerpts, v3 Appendices B–D provide cache storage and kernel details, complete collaboration and baseline prompts, model-specific formatting, step-termination rules, dataset access and license information, hardware configurations, and compute accounting. Appendix H additionally documents judge prompts and preprocessing.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands the literature context. Section 2 adds APAR and learned adaptive parallel reasoning, while Section 3.4 and Appendix B position the implementation relative to Flash-Decoding, PagedAttention, and RadixAttention. New attention, distributed-inference, benchmark, model, and judge references broaden the discussion while retaining the central contrast with fixed collaboration frameworks.

P1.justification: The retained material is substantially reorganized: alternative cache layouts move to Appendix A, the main method emphasizes the selected cache structure, inference optimization receives a separate subsection, and experiments are divided into four subsections. The discussion is rewritten with explicit limitations and future work, and the appendices separate implementation, prompting, configuration, analyses, and examples.

P2.justification: v3 adds a query-rotation diagram, replaces the original main results display with three curve panels, and introduces multi-model benchmark grids, collaboration bars, runtime plots, and two timing tables. The original cache-layout diagram is retained and redrawn in Appendix A. Extensive boxed prompts and reorganized appendix displays also materially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 establishes preliminary feasibility chiefly with QwQ-32B and does not measure wall-clock benefits. v3 addresses these important gaps through broader evaluations, Skeleton-of-Thought comparisons, component controls, and actual accuracy-versus-time evidence in Appendix F. Detailed implementation and prompting documentation, together with concrete failure analysis, substantially improve reproducibility and applicability assessment. Unequal coding answer-generation allowances and subjective proprietary judging limit some comparisons, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and technical support.
